**Claim.** Yes. If two topologies $\tau_1, \tau_2$ on a set $X$ have the same ultrafilter convergence (i.e., an ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$ converges to $x$ in $\tau_1$ iff it converges to $x$ in $\tau_2$), then $\tau_1 = \tau_2$.

**Proof.**

Recall the standard characterization of closure via ultrafilter convergence in an arbitrary topological space $(X,\tau)$:

> $(\star)$ For every $A\subseteq X$ and $x\in X$,
> $$x\in \operatorname{cl}_\tau(A) \iff \text{there exists an ultrafilter } \mathcal{U} \text{ on } X \text{ with } A\in\mathcal{U} \text{ and } \mathcal{U}\to x.$$

Let us verify $(\star)$.

($\Leftarrow$) Suppose $\mathcal{U}\to x$ and $A\in\mathcal{U}$. If $x\notin\operatorname{cl}_\tau(A)$, then there is an open neighborhood $U$ of $x$ with $U\cap A=\varnothing$. Since $\mathcal{U}\to x$, every neighborhood of $x$ belongs to $\mathcal{U}$, so $U\in\mathcal{U}$. But $A\in\mathcal{U}$ too, hence $U\cap A\in\mathcal{U}$, contradicting $U\cap A=\varnothing\notin\mathcal{U}$ (an ultrafilter contains no empty set). So $x\in\operatorname{cl}_\tau(A)$.

($\Rightarrow$) Suppose $x\in\operatorname{cl}_\tau(A)$. Then every neighborhood $U$ of $x$ meets $A$, i.e. $U\cap A\neq\varnothing$. The family $\{U\cap A : U \text{ a neighborhood of } x\}$ has the finite intersection property (finite intersections of neighborhoods are neighborhoods, still meeting $A$), so by the ultrafilter lemma it extends to an ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}$. Then $A\in\mathcal{U}$ (since each $U\cap A\subseteq A$ and $\mathcal{U}$ is upward closed — more carefully, the filter generated contains $A$ because $U\cap A\in\mathcal{U}$ for all $U$ and $A\supseteq U\cap A$), and every neighborhood $U$ of $x$ satisfies $U\in\mathcal{U}$ (since $U\supseteq U\cap A\in\mathcal{U}$). Hence $\mathcal{U}\to x$. This establishes $(\star)$.

Now apply $(\star)$ to both topologies. Since $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ have the same ultrafilter convergence, the right-hand side of $(\star)$ is identical for $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$. Therefore

$$\operatorname{cl}_{\tau_1}(A)=\operatorname{cl}_{\tau_2}(A)\quad\text{for every }A\subseteq X.$$

A topology is determined by its closure operator: the closed sets are exactly the sets $F$ with $\operatorname{cl}(F)=F$, and the open sets are their complements. Equal closures $\Rightarrow$ equal closed sets $\Rightarrow$ equal open sets $\Rightarrow \tau_1=\tau_2$.

(Equivalently, one may argue directly with open sets: $U\in\tau$ iff for every $x\in U$ and every ultrafilter $\mathcal{U}\to x$, $U\in\mathcal{U}$; this too depends only on the convergence relation, giving $\tau_1=\tau_2$ directly.)

Hence two topologies with the same ultrafilter convergence are identical. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
